questions.q: What stays the same across periods in all three recurring journal types?
questions.explain: All three recurring journal types use the same accounts every period; what differs is how the amount is determined.

questions.q: In a Skeleton recurring journal, how is the amount determined each period?
options: It is calculated automatically by a formula
It is entered manually after the journal is generated
It is the same fixed amount every time
questions.explain: Skeleton journals keep fixed accounts but require the amount to be typed in manually each period.

questions.q: Which recurring journal type requires no amount to be typed in at all, period after period?
questions.explain: Standard recurring journals use the same accounts and the same amount every period — nothing is entered manually.

questions.q: Which of the following can a Formula recurring journal reference to calculate its amount?
options: Only the journal's source and category
Fixed amounts, account balances, actual or budget amounts, statistics, and period-to-date/year-to-date balances
questions.explain: Formula entries can combine fixed amounts with balances, statistics, and PTD/YTD figures from various periods.

questions.q: When would Formula be a better choice than Skeleton for a recurring entry?
options: When the amount never changes at all
When the amount is derivable from data already in the ledger, removing manual calculation
When the journal needs to skip validation
questions.explain: Formula is ideal when the amount can be computed from existing balances or statistics rather than manually calculated and typed.
